What is the structure of the PDF's object hierarchy, and what role does the Catalog object play?

The PDF's object hierarchy consists of: object 4 as the Catalog (/Type /Catalog), which references object 1 as the Pages tree root (/Pages 1 0 R). Object 1 is the Pages node (/Type /Pages) with /Count 1 and a /Kids array pointing to object 3. Object 3 is the actual Page (/Type /Page), which contains the content stream (object 5), resources (fonts and graphics state), MediaBox dimensions, and annotations. The Catalog is the top-level entry point that PDF readers use to navigate the entire document structure.

Which PDF specification version does this file conform to?

This file conforms to PDF version 1.4, which is identified by the '%PDF-1.4' marker appearing at the very beginning of the file. This header is a standard part of the PDF format and tells PDF readers and processors which version of the specification was used to create the document, ensuring proper rendering and compatibility.
